claims.text: The feedstock is gas-atomized, cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi high-entropy-alloy powder.
The powder particle-size range is 15–45 µm.
The proposed intervention is maintaining the PBF-LB build plate at 400 ± 10 °C throughout the build.
Build-plate preheating to 400 °C reduces thermal gradients in AlCrFeNiSi during PBF-LB.
Build-plate preheating to 400 °C reduces the solidification cooling rate.
The lower thermal gradient and cooling rate enable greater in-situ diffusional homogenization during solidification.
Greater in-situ diffusional homogenization diminishes solute segregation at dendrite boundaries.
Preheating reduces shrinkage mismatch and thereby mitigates residual stress and cracking.
Preheating yields a more uniform AlCrFeNiSi microstructure with fewer porosity and crack-type defects.
Relative to an otherwise identical unheated-plate PBF-LB build, preheating will reduce average residual stress by at least 20%.
Relative to the unheated baseline, preheating will reduce measured microsegregation amplitude by at least 30%.
Relative to the unheated baseline, preheating will increase room-temperature tensile elongation by at least 15%.
Relative to the unheated baseline, the yield-strength change will remain within ±5%.
The combined reductions in segregation, residual stress, cracking, and porosity improve tensile ductility and overall mechanical integrity.
The hypothesis is valid within a laser-power range of 150–250 W, scan-speed range of 600–1000 mm/s, and layer-thickness range of 25–35 µm.
The hypothesis is valid in argon at no more than 50 ppm oxygen and for tensile testing at 20–25 °C.
The proposed effect may not transfer to other HEA compositions, other additive-manufacturing methods, or substantially different preheat temperatures.
The hypothesis is extrapolated from preheating effects reported for other Ni-based and Fe-based HEAs.
No direct prior data are available for build-plate preheating of AlCrFeNiSi under the stated conditions.
